meta.generatedFrom: TypeScript (the parity contract — never regenerate from Rust)
meta.description: 100000 sequential steps — 1.2% innovations plus sparse news shocks drawn from ±0.25 — deliberately wider than DAILY_SHOCK_CAP, so the shock clamp fires on roughly a third of shock days.
notes: INPUTS ARE RECORDED EXPLICITLY. They were produced by a seeded GameRng, but the Rust harness must read them from this file rather than regenerate them, so that a PRNG bug cannot masquerade as a mispricing bug.
sPrev is NOT recorded per step because it is exactly s[i-1] by construction (and initialState.s at step 0). The checker asserts that identity.
`outputSBits` may be an array of bits strings, or `{ constantBits, length }` when every element is identical. `innovations` and `shocks` use the same encoding.
A Rust harness should report the FIRST index at which outputSBits disagrees, plus the magnitude of the disagreement at each subsequent decade. A divergence index, not a boolean.
meta.floatEncoding: bits = raw IEEE-754 f64, big-endian, 16 uppercase hex digits. dec = shortest round-trip decimal, informational only.
meta.nanPolicy: Every NaN is recorded as 7FF8000000000000 (the pattern of Rust f64::NAN). V8 does not emit a stable NaN sign/payload, so only NaN-ness is contractual — compare NaN results with is_nan(), not with bits.
